description: Reference catalog of ecclesial communities for tracing breakaway lineages from the Catholic Church, including groups at separation_degree > 1. Only breakaway (or carefully marked synthetic/contested) nodes appear in `groups`. Communion bodies such as Eastern Catholics are listed under `excluded_non_breakaways`, not as breakaways.

root.name: Catholic Church
root.notes: Root node for lineage distance. Not a breakaway.

schema.name: display name
schema.separation_degree: shortest primary lineage distance from catholic-church
schema.lineage: ordered ids from catholic-church to this group
schema.notes: Lineages for restorationist/charismatic/AIC bodies are sometimes heuristic.

preference: Prefer durable communal identities. Mark contested cases. Synthetic nodes must not imply a false schism. Degree follows the primary broke_from chain. For each breakaway, prefer a concrete council locus; otherwise summarize. Eastern Catholics and other in-communion bodies are excluded from `groups`.

groups.name: Novatianists
groups.summary: Rigorist schism over lapsi; lasting parallel hierarchy for centuries.

disagreement.summary: Rejected readmission of the lapsed and formed a rigorist parallel hierarchy; Nicaea I canon 8 regulates reception of ‘Cathari’ (Novatianist) clergy into the Catholic Church without endorsing the schism.

groups.name: Melitian schism (Egypt)
groups.summary: Egyptian rigorist schism contemporary with early Arian controversies.

disagreement.summary: Egyptian rigorist schism over discipline of the lapsed and episcopal legitimacy; Nicaea’s synodal letter to Alexandria regulates Melitian clergy without accepting the schism’s claims.
disagreement.canonical_citation: Nicaea I Synodal Letter to the Church of Alexandria

groups.name: Donatists
groups.summary: North African rigorist church rejecting traditor clergy and Catholic episcopal legitimacy.

disagreement.summary: Denied the validity of sacraments and ordinations performed by traditores (clergy who had handed over scriptures in persecution); rejected Catholic bishops as compromised. No dedicated ecumenical-council decree on Donatism is in this corpus (settled mainly via African synods / Augustine).

groups.name: Arian churches
groups.summary: Communities and royal churches refusing Nicene homoousios; Homoean/Arian ecclesial structures among Goths, Vandals, Lombards.

disagreement.summary: Denied that the Son is consubstantial (homoousios) with the Father; rejected the Nicene Creed’s definition of the Son’s full divinity.

groups.name: Church of the East (Assyrian Church of the East)
groups.region: Persian Empire / East Syria / Central Asia / China (historical)
groups.summary: East Syriac dyophysite patriarchate that did not accept Ephesus’s condemnation of Nestorius; modern English name often ‘Assyrian Church of the East’.

disagreement.summary: East Syriac dyophysite patriarchate that did not accept Ephesus’s condemnation of Nestorius; commonly called the Assyrian Church of the East in modern English.
disagreement.canonical_citation: Ephesus, Third Epistle of Cyril to Nestorius (Cum salvator noster)

related_loci.canonical_citation: Ephesus, Epistle of Cyril to Nestorius (Intelligo quosdam)

groups.notes: Canonical id for this communion. ‘Assyrian Church of the East’ is the usual modern name, not a separate breakaway.

groups.name: Armenian Apostolic Church
groups.summary: National church rejecting Chalcedon; later Florence union attempt with Armenians.

disagreement.summary: Armenian church’s non-reception of Chalcedon; later Florence session 8 sought reunion on Catholic terms that were not lastingly received as ending the schism.

related_loci.note: Later reunion bull for Armenians (Florence S8) in corpus; primary doctrinal break remains Chalcedon.

groups.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
groups.summary: Alexandrian miaphysite patriarchate after Chalcedon; head of much African Oriental Orthodoxy.

disagreement.summary: Alexandrian non-reception of Chalcedon’s two-nature Definition; continuity with miaphysite confession after 451.

groups.name: Syriac Orthodox Church
groups.summary: West Syriac miaphysite patriarchate of Antioch (Jacobite).

disagreement.summary: West Syriac non-reception of Chalcedon’s two-nature Definition after 451.

groups.name: Eastern Orthodox churches
groups.summary: Byzantine-rite autocephalous churches out of full communion with Rome after the East–West schism.

disagreement.summary: East–West rupture over papal primacy, the Filioque, and related Latin practices; Florence’s union definition (Laetentur Caeli / session 6) and Lyons II’s reunion profession were not lastingly received in the Byzantine East.
disagreement.canonical_citation: Florence (Florence) S6 [Definition of the holy ecumenical synod of Florence]

related_loci.canonical_citation: Lyons II, Profession of Faith of Michael Palaeologus (Denzinger 461)

groups.name: Waldensians
groups.summary: Poor of Lyons dissenting movement forming lasting communities; later joined Reformed Protestantism.

disagreement.summary: Lay preaching and apostolic poverty outside episcopal authorization; Lateran IV’s anti-heresy constitution anathematizes dissent from the Catholic faith and orders episcopal/secular action against heretics and their supporters.

related_loci.note: Waldensian break is also disciplinary (unauthorized preaching); const. 3 is the council’s general heresy regime.

groups.name: Wycliffites / Lollards
groups.summary: English Wycliffite/Lollard reform networks condemned at Constance.

disagreement.summary: Condemned for Wyclif’s articles on the Eucharist, dominion, scripture, and church authority; Constance sentenced his teaching and memory.

related_loci.canonical_citation: Constance S15 [Articles of John Wyclif selected from the 260]

groups.name: Hussites
groups.summary: Bohemian reform communion after Hus; Utraquist and Taborite wings.

disagreement.summary: Bohemian reform after Hus: utraquism, critique of indulgences and papal power; Constance condemned Hus and his articles.

related_loci.canonical_citation: Constance S15 [Condemned articles of J. Hus]

groups.name: Lutheran churches
groups.summary: Evangelical churches of the Augsburg Confession rejecting papal jurisdiction and Tridentine soteriology/sacraments.

disagreement.summary: Justification by faith apart from Catholic scholastic accounts of merit; rejection of papal jurisdiction and several sacramental/Mass teachings defined against the Reformers at Trent.

related_loci.canonical_citation: Trent S4 Decree concerning the Canonical Scriptures
Trent S22 Doctrine on the Sacrifice of the Mass ch. 1

groups.name: Reformed / Calvinist churches
groups.summary: Magisterial Reformed communions (Zwinglian/Calvinist) rejecting Roman jurisdiction and Catholic sacramental order.

disagreement.summary: Rejection of papal jurisdiction, Catholic sacrificial Mass, and Trent’s sacramental system; strong emphasis on absolute divine sovereignty and reformed eucharistic teaching.
disagreement.canonical_citation: Trent S22 Doctrine on the Sacrifice of the Mass ch. 1

groups.name: Anabaptist / Radical Reformation churches
groups.region: Central Europe; later North America / global
groups.summary: Radical Reformation bodies practicing believers’ baptism and often separation from magisterial churches.

disagreement.summary: Believers’ baptism, separation of church from magisterial coercion, and rejection of infant baptism / state-church patterns shared by Catholics and magisterial Protestants.
disagreement.canonical_citation: Trent S7 Sacraments in General canon 1

related_loci.note: Trent defends Catholic sacramental order; Anabaptist break is also vs magisterial Reformation.

groups.name: Anglican Communion / Church of England
groups.summary: English national church rejecting papal jurisdiction; later Anglican Communion provinces.

disagreement.summary: Royal/national rejection of papal jurisdiction (1534) and later Protestant formularies; Trent addresses shared Reformational doctrinal disputes rather than the English Act of Supremacy itself.

related_loci.note: Jurisdictional break is the 1534 Act of Supremacy (not in this council corpus).

groups.name: Petite Église (anticoncordataires)
groups.summary: Clergy and faithful who refused the 1801 Concordat between Napoleon and Pius VII (and related reorganizations), maintaining a small separated ‘Little Church’ in parts of France and neighboring regions.
groups.notes: Historical remnant communities; not to be confused with later Independent Catholic bodies. Durable enough for cataloguing; largely faded as an organized communion.

disagreement.summary: Rejected the Concordat settlement and papal/civil reorganization of French dioceses, continuing a parallel anticoncordataire hierarchy and congregations.

groups.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
groups.summary: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints founded by Joseph Smith as a restoration of primitive Christianity, not as a schism from the Stone–Campbell Restoration Movement.
groups.notes: Prior broke_from=restoration-movement was historically false (parallel American restorationism, not a Campbellite split). Graph parent is catholic-church as the communion the movement claims was lost in apostasy; self-understanding is restoration, not Protestant denominational schism. confidence=contested for ‘breakaway’ typology.

disagreement.summary: Restorationist church founded by Joseph Smith (1830), claiming restoration of primitive Christianity after a universal apostasy—not a schism from the Stone–Campbell Restoration Movement.

groups.name: Old Catholic churches (Union of Utrecht)
groups.summary: Communions rejecting Vatican I papal infallibility/primacy definitions.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Vatican I’s definition of the Roman pontiff’s universal jurisdiction and ex cathedra infallibility.

groups.name: Polish National Catholic Church
groups.summary: Independent Catholic jurisdiction among Polish immigrants; historically allied with Old Catholics.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Roman episcopal control over Polish immigrant parishes (property, language, appointment of pastors); formed an independent Catholic-style jurisdiction.

groups.name: Philippine Independent Church (Aglipayan)
groups.summary: National church separating from Rome under Gregorio Aglipay amid colonial transition.

disagreement.summary: National church independence from Spanish/Roman hierarchy amid Philippine revolution and colonial transition; rejected continued Roman jurisdiction.

groups.name: Mariavite Church (Old Catholic Church of the Mariavites)
groups.summary: Polish Catholic renewal movement around Feliksa Kozłowska; suppressed and leaders excommunicated (1906), then organized as an independent church (later allied with Utrecht Old Catholics; majority body based in Płock).
groups.notes: Papal encyclical Tribus Circiter (1906) and Holy Office acts condemn the movement; those texts are not in the Step 1 council corpus. 1935 internal split produced the smaller Catholic Mariavite Church (Felicjanów).

disagreement.summary: Rejected Roman suppression of the Mariavite congregation and excommunication of its leaders (1906), forming an independent hierarchy after failed appeals to Rome.

groups.name: Iglesia ni Cristo
groups.summary: Restorationist church founded by Félix Manalo (registered 1914). Independent of the Philippine Independent Church; Manalo rejected Aglipayan doctrine as still essentially Catholic.
groups.notes: Prior catalog parent philippine-independent was incorrect. INC is a new restorationist body (Manalo had earlier Methodist and Adventist periods).

disagreement.summary: Restorationist church founded by Félix Manalo (1914), teaching a restored Church of Christ after apostasy; independent of Rome and of the Philippine Independent Church.

groups.name: Czechoslovak Hussite Church
groups.summary: Founded 8 January 1920 by reformist Roman Catholic clergy (Karel Farský et al.) after Vatican rejection of vernacular liturgy, voluntary celibacy, and related demands; claims Hussite heritage while originating as a Catholic clerical schism.
groups.notes: Not a direct organizational continuation of medieval Hussites (already catalogued); degree-1 parent is the Catholic Church.

disagreement.summary: Czech Catholic modernist clergy separated when Rome refused reform demands (vernacular Mass, optional celibacy, national church order), constituting the Czechoslovak (later Hussite) Church.

groups.name: Brazilian Catholic Apostolic Church
groups.summary: Independent Catholic church founded by Carlos Duarte Costa.

disagreement.summary: Bishop Duarte Costa’s break over Vatican political alignments and discipline; established an independent Catholic church with married clergy and vernacular liturgy.

groups.name: Chinese Catholic Patriotic Association structures
groups.summary: State-supervised Catholic structures with contested communion claims regarding Rome.
groups.notes: State-supervised Catholic structures; many participants still claim Catholic identity. Contested whether this is schism versus coerced jurisdictional control. Not a clean classic breakaway.

disagreement.summary: State insistence on episcopal appointment and church governance independent of Roman mandate; contested whether this is schism or coerced parallel structure.

groups.name: Sedevacantist independent chapels and societies
groups.summary: Bodies holding the post-conciliar Holy See vacant; separate sacramental networks (e.g. CMRI, SSPV).

disagreement.summary: Hold that recent claimants to the papal see lost office through heresy or vacancy; reject post-conciliar papal authority as illegitimate. No ecumenical decree defines against sedevacantism as such—disagreement is over who holds Peter’s office after Vatican II.

groups.notes: Hold the Holy See vacant and operate separate hierarchies/chapels. They claim to be the Catholic Church, not a new denomination; included as separated sacramental networks with contested typology.

groups.name: Palmarian Catholic Church
groups.summary: Conclavist church with its own papacy centered at El Palmar de Troya.

disagreement.summary: Private-revelation conclavism: elected an alternative papacy at El Palmar de Troya and rejected the Roman line after Paul VI.

groups.name: Unitas Fratrum / Moravian Church
groups.summary: Bohemian Brethren emerging from Hussite reform; renewed at Herrnhut as Moravian Church.

disagreement.summary: Further radicalization within the Hussite milieu toward a gathered ‘Unity of Brethren’ with distinct discipline and ministry—beyond Utraquist compromise with Rome.
disagreement.vs_parent: Separated from broader Hussite/Utraquist structures toward a stricter brotherhood model (later Moravian renewal).

groups.name: Hutterites
groups.summary: Communal Anabaptist tradition under Jakob Hutter.

disagreement.summary: Communal-goods Anabaptist discipline under Jakob Hutter; same radical-baptism rupture with Catholic sacramental order, expressed as a distinct brotherhood.
disagreement.vs_parent: Community of goods and Hutterite colony discipline vs other Anabaptist groups.

groups.name: Mennonite churches
groups.summary: Anabaptist tradition associated with Menno Simons; multiple conferences worldwide.

disagreement.summary: Anabaptist continuity under Menno Simons’ pastoral leadership—believers’ baptism and gathered-church discipline—distinct from Catholic and magisterial Protestant infant-baptism establishments.
disagreement.vs_parent: Organized Menno-Simons Anabaptist churches from the broader Radical Reformation stream.

groups.name: Presbyterian churches
groups.summary: Reformed churches with Presbyterian polity (e.g. Church of Scotland). Generally the Scottish/English form of the Reformed Reformation, not a later schism *from* continental Reformed churches.
groups.notes: Kept for tracing later American Presbyterian-linked movements (e.g. Restoration Movement leaders). Do not read broke_from=reformed as a 16th-c. secession event.

disagreement.summary: Reformed churches with Presbyterian polity (e.g. Church of Scotland)—typically the national form of the Reformed Reformation, not a later schism from continental Reformed churches.
disagreement.vs_parent: Polity/national expression within Reformed Protestantism (not a classic secession event).

groups.name: English Separatists / Congregationalists
groups.summary: Separatist and non-separating Puritan congregational churches leaving Anglican settlement.

disagreement.summary: Held that the Church of England remained insufficiently reformed; Separatists gathered autonomous congregations outside parish/episcopal structures.
disagreement.vs_parent: Congregational separation vs Anglican parish settlement.

groups.name: Remonstrant Brotherhood
groups.summary: Dutch Arminian (Remonstrant) churches organized after the Synod of Dort (1618–19) condemned the Remonstrant articles and expelled Arminian ministers from the Dutch Reformed Church.
groups.notes: Dort is a Reformed synod, not in the Catholic ecumenical council corpus. Lineage still traces Reformed → Catholic via the magisterial Reformation break.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Dort’s Calvinist condemnations of the five Remonstrant articles (conditional election, universal atonement, etc.) and formed a separate Remonstrant church.
disagreement.vs_parent: Arminian Remonstrant theology vs Synod of Dort / Dutch Reformed orthodoxy.

groups.name: Russian Old Believers
groups.summary: Split from Russian Orthodoxy over Nikonian liturgical reforms; popovtsy and bespopovtsy wings.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Patriarch Nikon’s liturgical reforms (sign of the cross, books, rites) as illegitimate corruption of Russian Orthodoxy.
disagreement.vs_parent: Nikonian ritual reform vs pre-reform Russian rite.

groups.name: Church of the Brethren (Schwarzenau Brethren)
groups.summary: Schwarzenau Brethren (German Baptists / Dunkers) formed 1708 under Alexander Mack with believers’ baptism and Anabaptist-Pietist practice; distinct from Mennonite conferences.
groups.notes: Parent anabaptist = Radical Reformation family; not a Mennonite conference schism.

disagreement.summary: Gathered a new believers’-baptism brotherhood at Schwarzenau with distinctive trine immersion and Pietist emphases alongside Anabaptist separationism.
disagreement.vs_parent: Schwarzenau Brethren identity vs other Anabaptist/Mennonite streams.

groups.name: Methodist churches
groups.summary: Wesleyan movement that formed separate churches from Anglican structures.

disagreement.summary: Wesleyan societies became a separate church with its own ordinations and conference polity, outside Anglican episcopal control.
disagreement.vs_parent: Conference ordination and connexional structure vs Church of England episcopacy.

groups.name: Swedenborgian / New Church
groups.summary: New Church / Swedenborgian bodies organized from the late 18th century, especially in England, on the basis of Emanuel Swedenborg’s writings.

disagreement.summary: New Church bodies organized especially in England on Emanuel Swedenborg’s revelations.
disagreement.vs_parent: Swedenborgian revelation vs Anglican/English Protestant orthodoxy (Swedenborg himself was Lutheran by background).

groups.notes: Swedenborg was a Lutheran by background; the institutional New Church is best attached here to the English/Anglican religious setting of its organization.

groups.name: Plymouth Brethren
groups.summary: Restorationist evangelical assemblies rejecting denominationalism; Open and Exclusive wings.

disagreement.summary: Rejected denominational clergy and formal membership for gathered open/exclusive assemblies under supposed New Testament pattern.
disagreement.vs_parent: Anti-denominational assembly fellowship vs Anglican/evangelical parish forms.

groups.name: Dutch Reformed secession churches (Afscheiding/Doleantie)
groups.summary: 19th-c. orthodox secessions from state Dutch Reformed Church; roots of CRCNA/Gereformeerde kerken.

disagreement.summary: Seceded from the Netherlands state church over doctrinal liberalism and church order (Afscheiding/Doleantie).
disagreement.vs_parent: Confessional orthodoxy and free-church order vs Nederlandse Hervormde Kerk.

groups.name: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod
groups.summary: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod organized (1847) by Saxon and other Lutheran immigrants in the U.S.; not founded as a schism from a single existing Lutheran synod abroad.

disagreement.summary: U.S. confessional Lutheran synod organized by immigrants (1847); confessional Lutheran identity rather than a schism from one European Lutheran church body.
disagreement.vs_parent: Immigrant confessional organization within Lutheranism (founding is not a secession decree from a parent synod).

groups.notes: broke_from=lutheran means confessional tradition parentage. Later LCMS fellowship disputes with other U.S. Lutherans are separate from the 1847 founding.

groups.name: Christian Reformed Church in North America
groups.summary: Dutch Reformed immigrants in Michigan seceded from the Reformed Church in America (1857), forming what became the Christian Reformed Church; linked to Afscheiding confessional concerns.
groups.notes: broke_from=reformed uses the Reformed family umbrella (immediate parent body: RCA). Related to Netherlands Afscheiding/Doleantie confessionalism already noted under dutch-reformed-splits.

disagreement.summary: Seceded from the Reformed Church in America over confessional laxity, Americanization, and Freemasonry concerns among Dutch seceder immigrants.
disagreement.vs_parent: Confessional Dutch seeder CRC vs RCA practice (1857).

groups.name: Community of Christ (RLDS)
groups.summary: Reorganized Latter Day Saint church under Joseph Smith III lineage.

disagreement.summary: Reorganized Latter Day Saint succession under Joseph Smith III, rejecting Brigham Young’s Utah leadership and later polygamy.
disagreement.vs_parent: Lineal succession and rejection of Utah LDS developments.

groups.name: Church of Christ (Temple Lot)
groups.summary: Hedrickite Latter Day Saint body rejecting Brigham Young and plural marriage; claims the Independence Temple Lot and a restored church without Utah LDS developments.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Utah LDS leadership, temple theology as developed in Utah, and plural marriage; organized under Granville Hedrick with Temple Lot claims.
disagreement.vs_parent: Hedrickite Temple Lot succession vs Brighamite LDS (Utah) leadership.

groups.name: Reformed Episcopal Church
groups.summary: Evangelical Anglican body founded by Bishop George David Cummins and others leaving the Protestant Episcopal Church over ritualism and catholicizing trends.
groups.notes: broke_from=anglican denotes the Anglican/Episcopal communion umbrella (specifically PECUSA).

disagreement.summary: Rejected advancing ritualism and exclusive sacramental claims in the Episcopal Church; organized a Reformed Episcopal jurisdiction with evangelical Anglican formularies.
disagreement.vs_parent: Evangelical/low-church protest vs ritualist trajectory in the Episcopal Church (1873).

groups.name: Evangelical Covenant Church
groups.summary: Swedish Mission Covenant / Mission Friends free-church movement arising from Lutheran revivalism; American Evangelical Covenant Church continues that stream.
groups.notes: Parent lutheran = state-church Lutheran context of the Mission Covenant secession.

disagreement.summary: Formed a free Mission Covenant church emphasizing conversion, Bible, and congregational mission outside the Lutheran state-church establishment.
disagreement.vs_parent: Free-church Mission Covenant identity vs Swedish/American Lutheran establishment.

groups.name: Jacobite Syrian Christian Church (Malankara)
groups.summary: Malankara church under the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch (Jacobite Syrian Christian Church), as distinct from the autocephalous Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

disagreement.summary: Malankara congregations under the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch (Jacobite Syrian Christian Church), distinct from the autocephalous Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.
disagreement.vs_parent: Remains under Antiochene patriarchal jurisdiction (not a secession from MOSC).

groups.notes: Not a breakaway *from* the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church; both parties contest succession within Malankara. Catalog parent is syriac-orthodox (patriarchal jurisdiction).

groups.name: Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church
groups.summary: Indian Orthodox church of West Syriac liturgy that asserted autocephaly vis-à-vis the Syriac Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch (1912).

disagreement.summary: Indian West Syriac Orthodox autocephaly vis-à-vis the Syriac Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch (1912).
disagreement.vs_parent: Autocephaly / catholicate independence from the Syriac Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch.

related_loci.note: Shared miaphysite non-reception of Chalcedon with the Syriac Orthodox parent tradition.

groups.notes: Earlier Malankara Christianity has layered East/West Syriac and colonial history; primary modern broke_from for this body is syriac-orthodox (autocephaly dispute).

groups.name: Liberal Catholic Church
groups.summary: Theosophically influenced independent sacramental church deriving orders via Old Catholic lines.
groups.notes: Degree 2 via Old Catholic succession; not a direct Roman doctrinal council break.

disagreement.summary: Combined Catholic sacramental forms with Theosophical freedom of belief, outside Roman and Utrecht Old Catholic doctrinal limits.
disagreement.vs_parent: Theosophical doctrinal liberty vs Old Catholic/Roman dogma.

groups.name: Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia (ROCOR)
groups.summary: Emigré Russian Orthodox jurisdiction; reconciled with Moscow Patriarchate in 2007 though some splinters remain separate.
groups.notes: Émigré Russian Orthodox jurisdiction formed amid Bolshevik-era disruption; conflict was with the Moscow Patriarchate’s situation, not a rejection of Eastern Orthodoxy as such. broke_from=eastern-orthodox is an umbrella parent.

disagreement.summary: Emigré refusal to submit to the Moscow Patriarchate under Soviet control; contested after 2007 reconciliation.
disagreement.vs_parent: Canonical submission to Moscow vs independent émigré synod.

groups.name: Greek Old Calendarists
groups.summary: Greek jurisdictions rejecting the Revised Julian calendar; subset of True Orthodox phenomenon.

disagreement.summary: Greek jurisdictions that refused the 1924 calendar change in the Church of Greece.
disagreement.vs_parent: Revised Julian calendar introduction.

groups.name: True Orthodox / Old Calendarist churches
groups.summary: Jurisdictions rejecting mainstream Orthodox calendar reforms and/or perceived ecumenism.

disagreement.summary: Reject mainstream Orthodox adoption of the Revised Julian calendar and/or participation in ecumenical dialogue as betrayal of Orthodoxy.
disagreement.vs_parent: Calendar reform and ecumenism within Eastern Orthodoxy.

groups.name: Aladura churches
groups.summary: Yoruba prayer-healing (Aladura) churches in Nigeria emerging from Anglican and other Protestant mission settings (e.g. Christ Apostolic Church, Cherubim and Seraphim).

disagreement.summary: Yoruba Aladura prayer-healing churches emerging from Anglican and related Protestant mission settings in Nigeria.
disagreement.vs_parent: Prophetic-healing independence from Anglican/mission church forms.

groups.notes: Parent anglican = primary mission context; some bodies have Methodist links.

groups.name: Catholic Mariavite Church (Felicjanów)
groups.summary: Minority Mariavite body that remained with Archbishop Kowalski after the 1935 deposition dispute; headquartered at Felicjanów.

disagreement.summary: Split from the Płock Mariavite majority over Kowalski’s leadership and doctrinal/disciplinary innovations.
disagreement.vs_parent: Loyalty to Kowalski and Felicjanów line vs Płock Old Catholic Mariavite majority (1935).

groups.name: Evangelical Free Church
groups.summary: Free-church evangelical tradition with Scandinavian Lutheran free-church ancestry.

disagreement.summary: Scandinavian free-church evangelicalism: congregational, conversionist, outside state Lutheran churches.
disagreement.vs_parent: Free-church polity vs state Lutheran establishment.

groups.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
groups.approx_rupture: Coptic jurisdiction → autocephaly 1959 (miaphysite via Alexandria after 451)
groups.summary: Tewahedo church historically under the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria; autocephalous since 1959. Miaphysite identity via Coptic / non-Chalcedonian lineage.

disagreement.summary: Miaphysite Tewahedo church under Coptic oversight after Chalcedon; modern autocephaly from the Coptic Orthodox Church (1959).
disagreement.vs_parent: Autocephaly and patriarchal independence from the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria (1959).

related_loci.note: Ancestral dogmatic non-reception of Chalcedon is via Coptic / Oriental Orthodox lineage, not a separate Ethiopian council act in 451.

groups.notes: broke_from=coptic-orthodox is jurisdictional/autocephalous history. Dogmatic separation from Catholic/imperial Chalcedonian communion is inherited via Coptic Orthodoxy.

groups.name: Ancient Church of the East
groups.summary: Calendar/jurisdiction split from the Assyrian Church of the East.
groups.notes: Broke from Church of the East (degree 1 from Catholic), not from Oriental Orthodox. Id normalized from oriental-orthodox-assyrian-split (not an Oriental Orthodox body).

disagreement.summary: Split from the Assyrian Church of the East over calendar reform and patriarchal jurisdiction (1968).
disagreement.vs_parent: Gregorian calendar adoption and related governance.

groups.name: Continuing Anglican churches
groups.summary: Jurisdictions leaving Canterbury/ECUSA Communion over prayer book, ordination, and doctrinal changes (Congress of St. Louis).

disagreement.summary: Rejected 1970s Prayer Book/ordination changes in ECUSA/Anglican Communion as departing from historic Anglican faith and order.
disagreement.vs_parent: 1970s liturgical and ordination changes.

groups.notes: Continuing churches after the 1977 Congress of St. Louis, chiefly from The Episcopal Church / Anglican realignment — not a break from every Anglican province.

groups.name: Anglican Church in North America
groups.summary: Realignment province formed by conservatives leaving The Episcopal Church / ACC.

disagreement.summary: Conservatives left TEC/ACC over sexuality, authority, and doctrine, forming a realignment province.
disagreement.vs_parent: Sexuality/doctrine disputes within North American Anglicanism.

groups.notes: Formed by conservatives leaving The Episcopal Church and Anglican Church of Canada (and related realignments). broke_from=anglican = Anglican Communion umbrella.

groups.name: Unitarian / Unitarian Universalist churches
groups.summary: Anti-Trinitarian and later liberal Protestant churches. Anglo-American Unitarianism grew mainly from Congregational/Separatist settings; Transylvanian Unitarianism is an earlier, separate continental stream.
groups.notes: broke_from=puritan-separatists tracks the Anglo-American story used elsewhere in this catalog; Transylvanian Unitarian Church is not a child of English Separatism.

disagreement.summary: Anti-Trinitarian and later liberal Protestant churches; Anglo-American Unitarianism grew mainly from Congregational/Separatist settings (Transylvanian Unitarianism is a separate early stream).
disagreement.vs_parent: Doctrinal liberalization / anti-Trinitarian identity within English-speaking Congregational-Separatist Protestantism.

groups.name: Baptist churches
groups.summary: Believers’-baptism churches emerging from English Separatism (General/Particular Baptists); later global family.
groups.notes: Some historians also stress continental Anabaptist influence; primary English lineage via Separatism.

disagreement.summary: Restricted baptism to believers (often by immersion) and gathered regenerate church membership, against infant baptism in Separatist/Anglican practice.
disagreement.vs_parent: Believers’ baptism and regenerate church membership.

groups.name: Religious Society of Friends (Quakers)
groups.summary: Fox’s Friends movement arising in the English Civil War religious ferment.

disagreement.summary: Rejected outward sacraments, paid clergy, and set liturgy in favor of the inward light and silent worship.
disagreement.vs_parent: Inward light vs Separatist/Puritan sacramental and clerical forms.

groups.name: Amish
groups.summary: Jakob Ammann split from Swiss Mennonites over discipline and shunning.

disagreement.summary: Jakob Ammann’s stricter ban (Meidung) and shunning practices split Swiss Mennonite communities; disagreement is disciplinary rigor within Anabaptism, not a new council-level doctrine vs Rome.
disagreement.vs_parent: Stricter shunning and footwashing discipline vs Swiss Mennonite practice (1693).

groups.name: Restoration Movement (Stone–Campbell)
groups.summary: American restorationists seeking New Testament church pattern; Churches of Christ / Christian Churches / Disciples.

disagreement.summary: Sought to restore New Testament church pattern, rejecting creeds and denominational names as divisive.
disagreement.vs_parent: No-creed restorationism vs Presbyterian/denominational Protestantism.

groups.name: Primitive Methodist Church
groups.summary: Hugh Bourne / William Clowes camp-meeting Methodists, excluded from Wesleyan Methodist Connexion structures, organized the Primitive Methodist Connexion (1811).

disagreement.summary: Continued open-air camp-meeting revivalism after Wesleyan Methodist authorities disciplined leaders; formed a separate Primitive Methodist connexion.
disagreement.vs_parent: Camp-meeting revivalism and lay intensity vs Wesleyan Methodist connexional control.

groups.name: African Methodist Episcopal Church
groups.summary: Black Methodist denomination founded by Richard Allen amid racial exclusion.

disagreement.summary: Black Methodists withdrew from white Methodist Episcopal control over seating and pastoral appointment (Allen).
disagreement.vs_parent: Racial exclusion and self-governance within Methodism.

groups.name: African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church
groups.summary: Independent Black Methodist body formed in New York.

disagreement.summary: Independent Black Methodist organization in New York amid similar racial barriers.
disagreement.vs_parent: Racial self-determination within Methodist structures.

groups.name: Catholic Apostolic Church (Irvingite)
groups.summary: Apostolic restorationist body associated with Edward Irving and the Albury circle; organized with restored ‘apostles’ (c. 1835). Grew from Church of Scotland / Presbyterian and broader Protestant apocalyptic circles.
groups.notes: confidence=contested for single-parent simplicity: Irving was Church of Scotland; English participants included Anglicans. broke_from=presbyterian tracks Irving’s church. The original CAC largely ceased as apostles died; New Apostolic Church is the main living fork.

disagreement.summary: Taught a restored apostolate and charismatic order beyond historic Presbyterian/Anglican ministry, organizing the Catholic Apostolic Church.
disagreement.vs_parent: Restored apostles and prophetic office vs Presbyterian (and Anglican) ministry norms.

groups.name: Mar Thoma Syrian Church
groups.summary: Reformed Oriental/West Syriac church influenced by Anglican CMS; distinct from both Rome and Malankara Orthodoxy.

disagreement.summary: Reforming party in Malankara under Anglican CMS influence; accepted reformed liturgy/theology while remaining West Syriac in heritage.
disagreement.vs_parent: Anglican-influenced reform vs Malankara Orthodox traditionalism.

groups.name: Free Church of Scotland
groups.summary: Evangelical majority left the established Church of Scotland in the 1843 Disruption over spiritual independence and patronage, forming the Free Church of Scotland.
groups.notes: Parent presbyterian = Church of Scotland / Presbyterian establishment. Later Free Church history includes the 1900 United Free merger and a continuing Free Church remnant.

disagreement.summary: Rejected state intrusion via patronage and defended the spiritual independence of the church, leaving the establishment in the Disruption of 1843.
disagreement.vs_parent: Spiritual independence / anti-patronage Free Church vs established Church of Scotland.

groups.name: Wesleyan Church
groups.summary: Wesleyan-Holiness denomination with roots in abolitionist Methodist splits.

disagreement.summary: Abolitionist and Holiness Methodist secession emphasizing freedom from episcopal Methodist compromises on slavery and sanctification.
disagreement.vs_parent: Abolition + Holiness emphases vs MEC practice.

groups.name: Exclusive Brethren (Darbyite)
groups.summary: Darbyite Exclusive assemblies separating from Open Brethren.

disagreement.summary: Darbyite exclusivism: tight disciplinary separation from Open Brethren and other Christians.
disagreement.vs_parent: Exclusive table fellowship and Darbyite discipline.

groups.name: Free Methodist Church
groups.summary: Holiness Methodist split emphasizing free pews and sanctification.

disagreement.summary: Opposed rented pews and lax discipline; Holiness revival within a free Methodist free-church form.
disagreement.vs_parent: Free pews, Holiness, and anti-slavery free Methodism.

groups.name: Salvation Army
groups.summary: Booth’s Wesleyan mission that became a distinct quasi-military church organization.

disagreement.summary: Booth’s mission adopted a quasi-military structure and largely set aside ordinary sacramental practice, separating from Methodist connexional forms.
disagreement.vs_parent: Military polity and non-sacramental mission methods.

groups.name: Holiness movement churches
groups.summary: Wesleyan-holiness denominations emphasizing entire sanctification (e.g. Church of the Nazarene roots, Pilgrim Holiness).

disagreement.summary: Taught a distinct experience of entire sanctification beyond mainstream Methodist practice; formed separate Holiness denominations.
disagreement.vs_parent: Entire sanctification as a second definite work of grace; stricter lifestyle rules.

groups.name: Christian Methodist Episcopal Church
groups.summary: Black Methodist church organized from the Methodist Episcopal Church, South.

disagreement.summary: Organized from the Methodist Episcopal Church, South after emancipation as a separate Black Methodist body.
disagreement.vs_parent: Post-emancipation separate Black Methodist jurisdiction.

groups.name: Old Order Mennonites
groups.summary: Mennonite groups that refused progressive innovations (meetinghouses, revivalism, later technology) and retained older Ordnung discipline; distinct from the Amish though parallel in conservatism.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Mennonite progressivism in worship, education, and later technology, preserving Old Order discipline and plain patterns.
disagreement.vs_parent: Old Order Ordnung vs progressive Mennonite conferences (from 1870s).

groups.name: Church of Christ, Scientist
groups.summary: Church of Christ, Scientist founded by Mary Baker Eddy (1879) in New England Protestant culture; not a clean jurisdictional schism from a single denomination.
groups.notes: broke_from=puritan-separatists is a cultural/lineage heuristic (Congregational New England), not a recorded congregational secession vote.

disagreement.summary: Mary Baker Eddy’s Church of Christ, Scientist (1879), arising in New England Protestant culture with a distinct metaphysics of healing and scripture interpretation.
disagreement.vs_parent: New religious movement in Congregational/New England Protestant culture (not a clean congregational secession).

groups.name: Christian and Missionary Alliance
groups.summary: Simpson’s deeper-life missionary movement becoming a denomination.

disagreement.summary: Simpson’s deeper-life and missionary emphasis organized into a distinct evangelical denomination.
disagreement.vs_parent: Alliance missionary/deeper-life identity vs Presbyterian home structures.

groups.name: Orthodox Presbyterian Church
groups.summary: Confessional Presbyterian church formed under J. Gresham Machen after conflict with the Presbyterian Church in the U.S.A. over modernism and foreign missions.
groups.notes: broke_from=presbyterian tracks PCUSA as the Presbyterian parent body.

disagreement.summary: Separated from the Presbyterian Church in the U.S.A. over doctrinal modernism and control of missions (Independent Board conflict), organizing the OPC.
disagreement.vs_parent: Confessional orthodoxy and independent missions vs PCUSA modernism (1936).

groups.name: United Church of Christ
groups.summary: US merger of Congregational Christian and Evangelical & Reformed churches.

disagreement.summary: Mid-20th-century merger creating a liberal mainline Protestant body from Congregational and German Reformed streams.
disagreement.vs_parent: Ecumenical merger identity (organizational, not a classical heresy dispute).

groups.notes: 1957 merger of Congregational Christian Churches and the Evangelical and Reformed Church. broke_from=puritan-separatists reflects only the Congregational side; E&R is German Reformed.

groups.name: Presbyterian Church in America
groups.summary: Conservative Presbyterian denomination formed chiefly from the Presbyterian Church in the United States (Southern) over biblical authority, confessional standards, and opposition to liberal trends.
groups.notes: broke_from=presbyterian umbrella; immediate parent body was PCUS.

disagreement.summary: Left the Presbyterian Church in the United States citing theological liberalism and departure from confessional Reformed standards, organizing the PCA.
disagreement.vs_parent: Confessional PCA vs PCUS liberalism (1973).

groups.name: Evangelical Presbyterian Church
groups.summary: Evangelical Presbyterian denomination formed mainly by congregations leaving the United Presbyterian Church / PC(USA) stream over theology, sexuality, and property/conscience issues, with an ‘essentials’ confessional approach.

disagreement.summary: Separated from mainline Presbyterian structures for evangelical orthodoxy and local-church liberty on contested ethical issues, forming the EPC.
disagreement.vs_parent: EPC evangelical essentials vs PC(USA)/UPCUSA mainline trajectory (1981).

groups.name: Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church
groups.summary: Autocephalous Oriental Orthodox church separated from Ethiopian Orthodox after Eritrean independence.
groups.notes: Degree 2 relative to Catholic via Ethiopian/Oriental Orthodox lineage.

disagreement.summary: Autocephaly from the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church after Eritrean independence—jurisdictional separation within Oriental Orthodoxy, not a new Christological disagreement with Rome.
disagreement.vs_parent: National autocephaly and patriarchal independence from Ethiopian Tewahedo structures (1993).

groups.name: Seventh Day Baptist churches
groups.summary: Sabbatarian Baptists; earlier than Seventh-day Adventists.

disagreement.summary: Observed the seventh-day Sabbath while remaining Baptist in baptism and congregational polity.
disagreement.vs_parent: Seventh-day Sabbath vs Sunday Baptist practice.

groups.name: Free Will Baptist churches (National Association of Free Will Baptists)
groups.summary: Arminian (‘General’ / Free Will) Baptist stream distinct from Particular/Calvinistic Baptists; northern and southern Free Will bodies united in the National Association of Free Will Baptists (1935).
groups.notes: broke_from=baptist as the believers’-baptism parent family. Free Will identity is doctrinal (general atonement, free will), not a single 1780 secession decree from one convention.

disagreement.summary: Affirmed general atonement and human free will against stricter Calvinistic Particular Baptist confessions, organizing lasting Free Will Baptist associations.
disagreement.vs_parent: Arminian Free Will Baptist theology vs Particular/Calvinistic Baptist orthodoxy.

groups.name: Millerite / Adventist movement
groups.summary: Second Great Awakening advent expectation; parent of Seventh-day Adventists and other advent bodies. Mixed Baptist/Christian Connexion roots.

disagreement.summary: Millerite imminent second-coming calculations and advent expectation after the Great Disappointment.
disagreement.vs_parent: Specific advent chronology and remnant identity vs Baptist/evangelical churches.

groups.name: Southern Baptist Convention
groups.summary: US Baptist split over slavery/missions organization; largest US Protestant denomination historically.

disagreement.summary: Southern US Baptists formed a separate convention over slavery and missions board control.
disagreement.vs_parent: Regional convention autonomy and slavery-era missions dispute.

groups.name: New Apostolic Church
groups.summary: Hamburg-centered continuation that called further apostles after conflict with remaining Catholic Apostolic apostles (1863); grew into the global New Apostolic Church.

disagreement.summary: Insisted on continuing to seal apostles beyond the original Catholic Apostolic college; organized separately after the Hamburg schism.
disagreement.vs_parent: Ongoing apostle calling (Hamburg) vs closed original Catholic Apostolic apostolate.

groups.name: Church of God (Anderson)
groups.summary: Holiness restorationist movement under D. S. Warner.

disagreement.summary: Warner’s ‘come-out’ Holiness restorationism rejected denominationalism while forming a distinct Church of God movement.
disagreement.vs_parent: Anti-denominational Holiness restoration vs existing Methodist/Holiness churches.

groups.name: Church of God (Cleveland, Tennessee)
groups.summary: Holiness church begun in the R. G. Spurling / A. J. Tomlinson stream (1886); became a major classical Pentecostal denomination after Azusa-era Spirit baptism teaching.

disagreement.summary: Organized a distinct Holiness (later Pentecostal) church government and doctrine of Spirit baptism apart from Methodist-Holiness parent bodies.
disagreement.vs_parent: Church of God (Cleveland) Holiness–Pentecostal order vs broader Holiness movement churches.

groups.name: Evangelical Friends Church International
groups.summary: Gurneyite / evangelical Friends who adopted programmed worship, pastors, and evangelical doctrine, distinct from silent unprogrammed Liberal/Hicksite Friends.
groups.notes: 1887 approximates major pastoral/programmed realignments; EFCI is the modern fellowship name.

disagreement.summary: Embraced evangelical Protestant orthodoxy and pastoral programmed worship against liberal/quietist Friends trajectories.
disagreement.vs_parent: Evangelical programmed Friends vs liberal/unprogrammed Quakerism.

groups.name: National Baptist Convention, USA
groups.summary: Major African American Baptist convention organized 1895 from earlier Black Baptist mission/publishing unions—parallel to white Baptist conventions rather than a single congregational secession.
groups.notes: confidence=contested for ‘breakaway’ typology: largely organizational consolidation under segregation, not a doctrinal anathema against a parent synod. Kept because it is the parent of later clear Baptist schisms (e.g. Progressive National Baptists).

disagreement.summary: Built independent Black Baptist national structures for missions, education, and publishing apart from white Baptist conventions.
disagreement.vs_parent: National Black Baptist convention autonomy vs white Baptist convention structures.

groups.name: Christian Church (Disciples of Christ)
groups.approx_rupture: 1906 (US Census recognition of Restoration three-way split)
groups.summary: Open-membership, instrumental Restoration wing that became the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ), distinguished from a cappella Churches of Christ after the early-20th-century Restoration division.

disagreement.summary: Accepted instrumental music, missionary societies, and broader open-membership practice within the Stone–Campbell movement, crystallizing as the Disciples of Christ.
disagreement.vs_parent: Disciples openness (instruments, societies, membership) vs stricter Restoration congregations.

groups.name: Churches of Christ (a cappella)
groups.summary: Conservative Restoration branch opposing instruments and missionary societies.

disagreement.summary: Opposed instrumental music and missionary societies within the Restoration Movement.
disagreement.vs_parent: A cappella worship and anti-society congregationalism.

groups.name: Pentecostal churches
groups.summary: Classical Pentecostal denominations emerging from Holiness revival (Azusa Street, etc.).

disagreement.summary: Affirmed tongues and gifts of the Spirit as normative evidence of Spirit baptism, beyond Holiness second-blessing teaching.
disagreement.vs_parent: Spirit baptism evidenced by speaking in tongues.

groups.name: Church of the Nazarene
groups.summary: Major Holiness denomination consolidated from Methodist-holiness bodies.

disagreement.summary: Consolidated Holiness bodies emphasizing entire sanctification and Wesleyan doctrine as a distinct denomination.
disagreement.vs_parent: Organized Holiness denominationalism from Methodist/Holiness streams.

groups.name: Kimbanguist Church
groups.summary: Church of Jesus Christ on Earth by the Prophet Simon Kimbangu; arose among Baptist-mission Christians in the Belgian Congo and became an independent AIC.

disagreement.summary: Simon Kimbangu’s Church of Jesus Christ on Earth, arising among Baptist-mission Christians in the Belgian Congo as an independent African church.
disagreement.vs_parent: Independent prophetic church from Baptist mission Christianity in Congo.

groups.notes: Parent baptist = mission context, not a formal Baptist denominational schism decree.

groups.name: Bible Methodist Connection of Churches
groups.summary: Conservative Holiness Methodist body formed by congregations leaving the Wesleyan Church over perceived relaxation of Holiness standards after mid-20th-century mergers.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Wesleyan Church compromises on Holiness lifestyle/standards and organized the Bible Methodist Connection.
disagreement.vs_parent: Conservative Holiness standards vs post-merger Wesleyan Church practice.

groups.name: Free Church of Scotland (Continuing)
groups.summary: Minority that left the Free Church of Scotland in 2000 amid worship and discipline controversies, claiming to continue historic Free Church practice.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Free Church Assembly decisions on worship/discipline as departing from historic Free Church standards; organized the Continuing Free Church.
disagreement.vs_parent: Continuing Free Church remnant vs Free Church of Scotland majority (2000).

groups.name: Advent Christian Church
groups.summary: Conditionalist Adventist denomination organized from Millerite advent believers who did not accept Seventh-day Adventist distinctive doctrines (Sabbath, EGW, sanctuary).

disagreement.summary: Continued adventist expectation with conditional immortality while rejecting Seventh-day Adventist Sabbath and prophetic claims as binding marks of the remnant.
disagreement.vs_parent: Advent Christian conditionalism vs emerging Sabbatarian Adventist (SDA) distinctives.

groups.name: Seventh-day Adventist Church
groups.summary: Sabbatarian Adventist denomination organized after the Great Disappointment.

disagreement.summary: Sabbatarian adventism with remnant theology, investigative judgment, and Ellen White’s prophetic role.
disagreement.vs_parent: Seventh-day Sabbath, sanctuary doctrine, and prophetic authority.

groups.name: Bible Student movement
groups.summary: Russell’s Bible Student movement emerging from adventist/restorationist milieu.

disagreement.summary: Russell’s chronological Adventism and rejection of mainstream church teaching on hell, Trinity, and organization.
disagreement.vs_parent: Russellite chronology and anti-Trinitarian trajectory from adventist milieu.

groups.name: American Baptist Association
groups.summary: Landmark Baptist fellowship organized after withdrawal from Southern Baptist Convention structures over local-church authority, closed communion, and opposition to centralized denominationalism (Baptist General Association → ABA).

disagreement.summary: Landmark ecclesiology: absolute local-church autonomy, Baptist succession claims, and refusal of ‘alien immersion’ / open pulpit practices associated with Convention Baptists.
disagreement.vs_parent: Landmark associational Baptists vs Southern Baptist Convention centralization (1905).

groups.name: Church of God in Christ
groups.summary: Major African American Pentecostal denomination under Charles H. Mason after Azusa Street; Holiness roots reorganized as Pentecostal COGIC.
groups.notes: Parent pentecostal = classical Pentecostal family. COGIC’s Holiness beginning (1897) predates the 1907 Pentecostal turn; catalog degree follows the Pentecostal identity.

disagreement.summary: Organized a distinct episcopal Pentecostal church (COGIC) emphasizing sanctification and Spirit baptism, separate from other Holiness and Pentecostal bodies.
disagreement.vs_parent: COGIC episcopal Pentecostal order vs other classical Pentecostal fellowships.

groups.name: Assemblies of God
groups.summary: Largest classical Pentecostal fellowship, organized at Hot Springs, Arkansas.

disagreement.summary: Organized Trinitarian Pentecostal fellowship with doctrinal statements on Spirit baptism and tongues.
disagreement.vs_parent: Denominational organization of classical Pentecostalism.

groups.name: Oneness Pentecostal churches
groups.summary: Non-Trinitarian Pentecostal bodies (e.g. UPCI) splitting from Trinitarian Pentecostalism.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Trinitarian baptismal formula and classical Trinitarian doctrine in favor of Jesus’-name Oneness teaching.
disagreement.vs_parent: Oneness vs Trinitarian Pentecostal theology.

groups.name: International Church of the Foursquare Gospel
groups.summary: Pentecostal denomination founded by Aimee Semple McPherson (1923) with the ‘Foursquare’ gospel emphasis; distinct from Assemblies of God and other classical bodies.

disagreement.summary: Organized a separate Foursquare Pentecostal denomination around McPherson’s Angelus Temple ministry and foursquare doctrinal formula.
disagreement.vs_parent: Foursquare denominational organization vs other classical Pentecostal fellowships.

groups.name: Christian Churches and Churches of Christ (Independent)
groups.summary: Conservative instrumental Restoration congregations that refused Disciples denominational structures and theological liberalism, remaining as Independent Christian Churches / Churches of Christ (not the a cappella Churches of Christ).
groups.notes: Date approximates North American Christian Convention / independent alignment period.

disagreement.summary: Rejected Disciples’ restructure and liberal theology while retaining instruments and remaining outside both the Disciples denomination and a cappella Churches of Christ.
disagreement.vs_parent: Independent Christian Church conservatism vs Disciples denominational liberalism/restructure.

groups.name: Grace Communion International (ex–Worldwide Church of God)
groups.summary: Armstrong’s Radio/Worldwide Church of God; later trinitarian evangelical reformation as GCI; splinters remain.

disagreement.summary: Armstrongism’s British-Israel and sabbatarian system; later GCI reformed toward evangelical Trinitarianism while splinters retained older teachings.
disagreement.vs_parent: Armstrongite doctrines (and later GCI’s break from them).

groups.name: Independent Charismatic / neo-Pentecostal networks
groups.summary: Post-classical charismatic megachurches and apostolic networks; many have mixed Protestant parentage.
groups.notes: Umbrella for independent charismatic networks; parentage is mixed (Pentecostal, Baptist, Reformed, and some Catholic charismatic). broke_from=pentecostal is a simplification.

disagreement.summary: Independent charismatic networks emphasizing apostolic/prophetic leadership and contemporary gifts outside classical Pentecostal denominations.
disagreement.vs_parent: Apostolic-prophetic independent structures vs classical Pentecostal denominations.

groups.name: Progressive National Baptist Convention
groups.summary: Black Baptist convention formed in 1961 by leaders leaving the National Baptist Convention, USA, amid disputes over civil-rights activism and presidential tenure limits.

disagreement.summary: Split from NBCUSA over support for the civil-rights movement and convention governance (tenure) conflicts.
disagreement.vs_parent: Progressive National Baptists’ civil-rights activism vs NBCUSA leadership stance (1961).

groups.name: Seventh Day Adventist Reform Movement
groups.summary: Sabbatarian Adventist reform body arising from World War I conflicts over military service and church discipline within European Seventh-day Adventism.

disagreement.summary: Charged the Seventh-day Adventist Church with compromising Sabbath and noncombatant principles in wartime; organized a Reform Movement.
disagreement.vs_parent: Reform Movement wartime/Sabbath discipline vs SDA official wartime policy.

groups.name: Jehovah’s Witnesses
groups.summary: Watch Tower society under Rutherford; distinct doctrines on Trinity, governance, eschatology.

disagreement.summary: Watch Tower teachings denying the Trinity, affirming a modern governing organization, and distinctive eschatology under Rutherford.
disagreement.vs_parent: Governing Body authority and non-Trinitarian Watch Tower doctrine.

groups.name: United Pentecostal Church International
groups.summary: Largest Oneness Pentecostal denomination, formed by merger of Pentecostal Church, Incorporated and Pentecostal Assemblies of Jesus Christ (1945).

disagreement.summary: Consolidated major Oneness Pentecostal organizations into UPCI with shared Jesus’-name baptism and non-Trinitarian confession.
disagreement.vs_parent: UPCI organizational merger within the Oneness Pentecostal family.

groups.name: Baptist Missionary Association of America
groups.summary: Landmark Baptist body formed in 1950 when churches left the American Baptist Association (initially North American Baptist Association; renamed BMAA).

disagreement.summary: Split from the American Baptist Association over associational authority, missions administration, and leadership conflicts while remaining Landmark in ecclesiology.
disagreement.vs_parent: BMAA associational/missions dispute vs ABA (1950).

groups.name: Calvary Chapel Association
groups.summary: Chuck Smith’s Calvary Chapel movement emerging from Foursquare/Pentecostal contexts into an independent charismatic-evangelical association with distinctive verse-by-verse teaching and Jesus Movement outreach.
groups.notes: confidence=contested: Smith’s path involved Foursquare credentialing/influence but Calvary Chapel is not a simple congregational secession vote from ICFG. Parent foursquare = nearest classical Pentecostal institutional context.

disagreement.summary: Developed an independent Calvary Chapel model (expositional preaching, balanced charismatic practice, association polity) outside Foursquare denominational structures.
disagreement.vs_parent: Calvary Chapel association model vs Foursquare denominational order.

groups.name: Vineyard Movement
groups.summary: Charismatic evangelical association founded by John Wimber et al.

disagreement.summary: Wimber’s ‘power evangelism’ charismatic evangelicalism organized apart from prior denominations.
disagreement.vs_parent: Signs-and-wonders charismatic practice in a distinct association.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: african-instituted-churches
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Scholarly category, not a parent church; Kimbanguist/Aladura reattached to concrete mission contexts.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: assyrian-church-of-the-east
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Duplicate naming of the same historic Church of the East patriarchate; canonical catalog id is church-of-the-east (Assyrian Church of the East is the common modern English name for that body).

excluded_non_breakaways.name: cathars
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Cathar/Albigensian networks are contested as a durable ‘church’; excluded under the formal breakaway definition (see root README / clean_breakaways).

excluded_non_breakaways.name: congregationalist-approx
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Synthetic milieu node, not a historical church people broke from.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: eastern-catholic-note
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Eastern Catholic churches (Byzantine, Maronite, Chaldean, Syro-Malabar, etc.) are in full communion with Rome; not breakaways.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: maronites-note
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Maronite Church is an Eastern Catholic church in full communion with Rome; not a breakaway.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: messianic-jewish
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Modern Messianic congregations are not a schism from Baptist churches; mixed evangelical parentage — removed rather than assert a false parent.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: oriental-orthodox
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Modern family name for non-Chalcedonian miaphysite churches. Not a church polity that groups broke from; dogmatic rupture is Chalcedon (see each national church). Tracked under family_labels when present.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: oriental-orthodox-twahedo-split-note
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Synthetic alias of eritrean-orthodox; removed as redundant.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: pietist-movements
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Pietism was largely an intra-Lutheran renewal; not a single durable separated communion.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: protestant-missions-umbrella
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Synthetic umbrella, not a church; children reattached to real parents.

excluded_non_breakaways.name: sspx
excluded_non_breakaways.reason: Society of St. Pius X claims Catholic identity and the same communion; Rome treats it as irregular, not a separate church. Excluded under the formal definition (rejecting implementation while claiming same communion).

family_labels.name: Oriental Orthodox churches
family_labels.reason: Modern family name for non-Chalcedonian miaphysite churches. Not a church polity that groups broke from; dogmatic rupture is Chalcedon (see each national church). Tracked under family_labels when present.
